matches.rationale: Both identify cherry-picked positive results, omission of negative cases, and unreliable reported improvements in the Experiments (Section 4/Table 2).
No finding addresses the inconsistent specification of the projection function ψ for ICL and other meta-learners in Sections 3.1 and 3.3.
No finding points out that using a common hyperparameter configuration for all learners ignores baseline tuning needs or lacks profiling of computational cost during meta-testing.
No finding addresses the Abstract's overstatement of seamless integration and significant boost without limitation hedges.
No finding mentions the omission of ethical/energy/environmental considerations in the Discussion.
Both expose that Theorem 1/Lemma 1 lack rigorous proof, rely on unjustified approximations, and fail to substantiate the claimed theoretical guarantees in Section 3.2 and Appendix B.
No finding highlights that the ablation on K and contrastive loss variants in Section 4.3 shows only partial, hand-picked results without variance or failure modes.
No finding captures the mismatch between the abstract's "problem- and learner-agnostic" claim and the method's reliance on episodic framework and task identity.
No finding criticizes the Related Work's mischaracterization of prior art and overstated novelty claim.
No finding addresses the conclusion's overly promotional language and lack of limitations.
Both target the same ambiguity in Section 3.1: the sampling strategy π_κ is not rigorously defined, hindering reproducibility of the inner-task distance computation.
No finding identifies the gap between synthetic ICL experiments in Section 4.4 and unsubstantiated claims about real‑world LLMs.
No finding points out that changes in backbone architecture confound the attribution of gains to ConML in Section 4.1/Appendix F.
Both highlight that the lambda sensitivity discussion in Section 4.3 contradicts an earlier downplaying of tuning difficulty, glossing over practical fragility.
No finding mentions the missing significance tests, confidence intervals, or number of trials in the reported tables.
